facts.text: TrifingerEnv is the concrete IsaacGym environment for the three-finger TriFinger robot
TrifingerEnv derives from IsaacEnvBase, the repository's own base class, not from gym.Env or gymnasium.Env
The default configuration sets episode_length to 750, command_mode to position, normalize_action to true and the object initial state to random
The robot has three fingers with three joints each, so the joint position, joint velocity and joint torque dimensions are 9
The joint position limits are [-0.33, 0.0, -2.7] to [1.0, 1.57, 0.0] per finger, the joint velocity limit is 10 rad/s and the maximum joint torque is 0.36 N m
The comment on normalize_action says the action is denormalized from [-1, 1], and the default value is true
The VecTask wrapper builds the action space as Box(-clip_actions, clip_actions) with clip_actions 1.0
step takes an action tensor of shape [num_instances, action_dim] and returns observation, reward, termination and info buffers
step resets the instances whose reset flag is set before applying the action, and sets that flag when the step count reaches episode_length
reset returns the observation tensor [num_instances, obs_dim]
The observation spec is robot_q 9, robot_u 9, object_q 7, object_q_des 7 and command 9, 41 values in total for the default action dimension
seed sets Python's random, NumPy and PyTorch seeds
The constructor seeds the environment from its config, whose default seed is 0
The default physics timestep is 0.02 s and control_decimation is 1, so one environment step advances 0.02 s
TrifingerEnv.__init__ takes config, device, verbose and visualize
The README states that the repository provides an IsaacGym environment for the TriFinger robot and that it supports IsaacGym Preview Release 2
The install requirements list numpy, scipy, gym, torch, hydra-core and rl_games, with no serial, VISA, USB or vendor hardware package

determinism.notes: TrifingerEnv.seed(seed) seeds Python's random, NumPy and PyTorch (env_base.py:312-320), and the default reset draws the object pose and goal from those generators (trifinger_env.py:66); the fake uses Python's random.Random and was never compared with the upstream environment

gaps: the fake backend is a pure Python stand-in: it models the tick, a placeholder nine-value joint offset and a placeholder 41-value observation row, but no IsaacGym, PhysX, rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuators or sensors, and it was never compared with the upstream environment
one cap.world.step.v1 tick is one TrifingerEnv.step call, which runs control_decimation physics steps (env_base.py:382-384); with the default control_decimation 1 and dt 0.02 s that is 20 ms per tick
the upstream is vectorized ([num_instances, obs_dim]); the fake models one instance and the driver returns its first observation row, so a configured num_instances above 1 is not exposed

only the default configuration is modelled (position command mode, normalized action, episode length 750); torque and position_impedance modes, asymmetric observations, force-torque sensors and rendering are not modelled
the upstream environment auto-resets an instance at episode_length (env_base.py:392-395); the driver reports truncated at 750 ticks and requires an explicit reset instead of continuing
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state
the real environment needs IsaacGym Preview Release 2, PyTorch and a config dict (README.md:7-17, trifinger_env.py:258-277); it was not installed or run where the gate ran
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against one
